text:
anya: Quick thought — we should start an interface contraction spike for the enrichment layer. The hotpath has ~7 tiny proxies and a bunch of adaptor shims that add latency and test-surface. Idea is to reduce surface area, collapse two thin proxies, and centralize auth checks. Thoughts?

matt: +1 on running a spike. can we scope it to a single tenant path first? reduce blast radius. :thumbsup:

li: Agree. Can you call out which proxies? my mental map: enricher-proxy, tenant-mux, telemetry-shim, model-adapter, feature-flag-proxy, rate-limit-facade, auth-sidecar.

anya: Yep that's the set. Proposal:
1) collapse tenant-mux + auth-sidecar into a single sidecar controlled by config
2) remove telemetry-shim (move minimal spans into router)
3) keep model-adapter but add a thin stable contract for kv cache access

cory: FWIW we should avoid changing the canonical request payload for the runtime. If we change it we force rollouts across Dedicated and Private. Better to adapt inside the proxies first, then flip a compatibility header.

anya: Good call. Plan for compatibility header flip: add `x-ri-contract-v` header, default v1.0, flip to v1.1 only after canary.

jen: Product ask: make sure this doesn't change per-tenant quota semantics. We need telemetry + billing continuity.

li: For the spike, recommend measuring 95th pct latency delta and token-cost delta. Also track tail-percentile errors during canary.

anya: I'll draft a short runbook and spike PR: scope 2 semaines, branch cut for tenant=test-1, automated canary to 10% traffic, fallback path to v1.0.

cory: Also add a checklist for Dedicated: config-push window, and Private deployments — we need manifest change notes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created spike branch `interface-contract-spike/anya` for env=staging. CI started.

matt: 👍 for staging branch. for rollouts, we should use runtime feature flags so we can toggle collapse without requiring infra redeploy.

li: Technical tradeoff: collapsing proxies reduces RPC hops (good) but centralizes failure domain. Need circuit-breakers and per-route timeouts.

anya: agreed — include hardened circuit-breakers, per-route concurrency caps, and a small autoscale target. I'll add a diagram to the PR showing failure domains.

jen: Any effect on SLAs? if we centralize auth, we may see auth-induced latency. Make sure we have fallback path (auth bypass token for emergency).

cory: keep a fallback policy but default off. Also add an alert on auth-latency > 200ms  p95.

anya: I'll add those alerts. Next steps: I'll open the RFC followup doc with spike plan, test matrix, metrics, and a cutover checklist. Expect PR today. Thanks all. :rocket:
